ariadneDB: the ariadne resource graph database

ariadneDB hosts a harmonised resource graph with feature mappings from various biological databases, powering the R package ariadne and its Python extension ariadnePy. A walkthrough on the available resources can be found in this vignette.

Resources

Resource graphs are stored in the Graph Modelling Language (GML) format for optimised graph representation. Each GML file corresponds to one source database and includes a graph:

  • edges link source features (from) with target features (to) and contain paths to mappings when available (url)
  • nodes list the available features with their ariadne names (name), database-specific names (specific) and self-generated identifiers (id)

Each resource graph is generated with a reproducible pipeline (found here) and gets regularly updated based on the release cycle of the respective source database.

Usage

The full ariadne database can be fetched via the ariadne library.

In R:

library(ariadne)

# Fetch resources
graph <- ariadne()

# Visualise resource graph
plotPath(graph)

In Python:

import ariadnepy

# Fetch resources
graph = ariadnepy.ariadne()

# Visualise resource graph
ariadnepy.plot_path(graph)

Alternatively, single GML files can be imported using the igraph library.

library(igraph)

# Set url
url <- "https://zenodo.org/records/18788726/files/ChocoPhlAn.gml"

# Import resource
graph <- read_graph(url, format = "gml")
